explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake or counterfeit, the opposite of genuine.

clue.text: Extra small advantage, bagging game when returning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run the opposite way
to bag something is to put it inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
RU is rugby union
a plus is an advantage

explanation.surface: A slight edge in a match, picked up on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: The game letters, turned round, go inside the small advantage, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Surplus is an amount left over beyond what is needed, so it means additional or extra.

clue.text: Running track with area later being examined

indicators.note: the letter for area is moved further along the word, so the order of its letters changes

blocks.note: a machine that is running is on
a track is a trail

explanation.surface: An athletics track, with its field area built later, is being inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the A of the track word one place later turns it into the court word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on trial is having their case heard in court, or a product is being tested, both forms of scrutiny.

clue.text: Primarily operatic cast performing this?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used
letters that are performing are put through their paces, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: What might an opera company mainly be staging?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: an opera cast could well be performing this work.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera of 1900, a staple of the repertoire for any opera company.

clue.text: Good vocalist almost has trouble around violinist

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut
turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a rapper vocalises, here missing the final letter
ill is trouble, as in ill fortune

explanation.surface: A decent singer nearly gets into difficulty with a fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal but here it turns the trouble word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stéphane Grappelli was the French jazz violinist who played with Django Reinhardt in the Quintette du Hot Club de France.

clue.text: Cult leader intoxicated media around strange site

indicators.note: strange means odd and out of the ordinary, so the letters fall into an odd order
around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: someone high is intoxicated
the press is the news media
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A drugged-up cult figure surrounded by reporters at a weird location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intoxicated' looks like it might signal rearrangement but simply gives a synonym; 'strange' is the real one.
explanation.definitionFit: A high priestess is the chief female priest of a cult or religion, so she leads its worship.

clue.text: I must leave music player in school

indicators.note: whatever must leave is taken away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written, the letter to go
Apple's portable music player

explanation.surface: A pupil must take their music player out of class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a classroom but is a group of whales or dolphins.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a group of whales or dolphins swimming together, as a school is a group of fish.

clue.text: Reportedly diaphanous coat is removed when people do this

definitions.text: coat is removed when people do this

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken out, so we want a word that sounds the same

blocks.note: diaphanous fabric is sheer, thin enough to see through

explanation.surface: A see-through coat is taken off when people do this.
explanation.walkthrough: The coat is a sheep's fleece, which shearers cut off; 'diaphanous' points to clothing to keep the picture on dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing a sheep removes its woolly fleece, its coat, in one piece with clippers.

clue.text: Boost the FBI in a case of underachievement

indicators.note: a case is the outer covering, so only the outside letters of the word are kept
in means inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters
G-men, government men, are FBI agents

explanation.surface: The FBI need a lift after a case where they fell short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' fits the police-investigation picture but means the outer letters; G-men is American slang for federal agents.
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to make something greater by adding to it, so it means boost.

clue.text: Idiot without skill by northern Scottish town

indicators.note: without can mean outside, so one piece stands around another

blocks.note: a dumbo is a stupid person
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool from a town up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking but is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a town on the River Clyde in west central Scotland, with a famous castle rock.
